title: Data & AI Practice Lead at Global Systems Integrator Expects Docusign Business to Grow 8%–10%, With IAM Supporting Retention and Upselling
expert: Data & AI practice lead at a global systems integrator and Docusign alliance partner (presales, implementation, integrations)
verdict: The expert's Docusign practice grew 8%–10% y/y in Aug–Oct 2026, with churn about 10% lower and more than 90% of new revenue from existing-customer expansion.

Back to double-digit growth: 🟡 Practice +8%–10% y/y in Aug–Oct, between the 2026-11-05 partner reads of about 5% and roughly 20%; still short of double digits. → Stance (double-digit growth) →
🔴 New logos under 10% of new revenue and 5%–7% of growth; first read. → Stance (double-digit growth) ↓
DBNR / renewal expansion: 🟢 Net retention slightly above 100%, churn about 10% lower, renewal spend +2%–3%; consistent with the page's DBNR of 101%. → Stance (retention) ↑
IAM adoption: 🟢 Over 90% of new revenue from expansion and IAM upsell; Cleveland saw IAM 3Q bookings slightly ahead (SB #63574): consistent. → Stance (IAM bet) ↑
🔴 CLM adoption +1%–2%; Cleveland saw CLM below expectations (SB #63588): consistent; vs 2026-11-05 PMO estimate of 8%–10%: lower. → Stance (IAM bet) ↓
Pricing & competition: 🟡 Pricing +1%–2%, in line with inflation, as large customers move to three-year contracts; vs the 2026-11-05 PMO's ~20% IAM-related price rise: lower. → Stance (margins) →

changes: Growth: practice +8%–10% vs 2026-11-05 partner reads of about 5% (EC-1000000-268443) and roughly 20% (EC-1000000-268577): in between.
CLM: adoption +1%–2% vs Cleveland CLM below expectations and net-new CLM deal volume down y/y (SB #63588): consistent.
Retention: net retention slightly above 100% vs the thesis page's DBNR of 101%: consistent.
Pricing: +1%–2% vs the 2026-11-05 PMO's ~20% IAM-related price rise on lower plans: lower.
thesis_impact: Stance (neutral; double-digit growth rests on IAM): → — 8%–10% practice growth with IAM driving over 90% of new revenue, but new logos are under 10% of new revenue and CLM is +1%–2%; supports 'not a short', not a re-acceleration.
